title: After-loop scratch: Laila Hassan — runtime candidate
content:
Candidate: Laila Hassan — Staff / Senior Principal level (inference/runtime)
Interviewer: Samira Patel (me) — runtime lead; Ethan Chen — SRE; Maya Singh — applied ML
Date: 2025-07-18 (loop) — quick personal scratchpad, not shared as-is

Top-line gut: leaning toward hire-with-reservations (strong systems + ops instincts; needs deeper micro-optimizations knowledge for KV/cache/quantization tradeoffs). Good communicator, pragmatic.

Quick summary bullets:
- Systems design + tradeoffs: excellent. Walked through multi-tenant GPU pool design, isolation boundaries, tenant QoS. Brought up preemption / scheduler fairness concrete heuristics.
- Latency debugging: concrete examples of using tail-latency sampling, p95/p99 instrumentation; proposed fallbacks (smaller model shard, reduced beams) — pragmatic and product-aware.
- ML inference knowledge: solid on batching and KV cache basics, weaker on low-level kernel/quantization details (Fp8/4-bit failure modes). Could learn but would need ramp time.
- Team/people fit: collaborative, asks about on-call rotation norms, docs culture, mentoring. Speaks product-first.
- Red flags: a few assumptions about memory-locality for sharded KV cache that don't hold on some interconnects; missed a corner-case about host-to-device memcpy overlap in our preferred runtime. Not fatal, but marks a gap.

Scores (my informal 1-5):
- Deep systems & infra design: 5
- ML inference kernel-level knowledge: 3
- Debugging & observability: 5
- Operational maturity (oncall/runbooks): 5
- Communication & cross-team: 4
- Ownership/instancing: 5

Question-by-question notes (shorthand):
- Warmup / intro (5m): clear background summary — lead infra at last company, moved inference from prod-binding infra to autoscale pools. Good examples.
- Multi-tenant scheduler prompt (25m): proposed weighted fair queueing by token-cost; suggested backpressure into frontend, graceful degradation tiers (cheap quantized model fallback). Thoughtful capacity planning calcs (SLA targets -> needed GPU count). Mentioned cost model but didn't deeply quantify per-token cost.
- KV cache/LLM caching (20m): sketch: per-tenant LRU + cold storage; suggested cache warmers, hot-key tracking. Missed async writeback strategy detail for KV consistency during eviction under preemption (we discussed, she agreed it needs careful locking).
- Kernel/quantization (15m): high-level familiarity with 4-bit quant, aware of perf/accuracy tradeoffs. Couldn't name specific packing kernels or reference libs beyond BigDL/TensorRT generalities.
- Incident postmortem (10m): great PM-style narrative. Drove to root cause, proposed monitoring hooks, and a canary rollout plan.

Concrete pros:
- Immediate value in infra design, SRE discipline, runbook creation, and cross-functional incident handling.
- Likely to improve our hosting/fallback playbook and rollout safety.

Concrete cons / hiring concerns:
- Not deep on low-level kernel tuning/quantization — would not be the one to implement custom fused kernels right away.
- Assumed some behaviors for sharded KV that don't match our NVLink topologies; would need to pair on a few areas.

Follow-ups & recommended loop actions:
- Consider a short pairing session with one of our inference engineers on a small kernel/quantization problem to validate ramp speed (30–60m pairing).
- Ask applied-ML interviewer to probe a small evaluation: can they design an A/B to measure quality drop for 4->3-bit quant for our benchmark (simple take-home)?
- If team wants to continue, suggest an onsite (or extended pairing) focusing on kernel tradeoffs + one debugging whiteboard.

Offer/level guidance (raw): Strong fit for Senior/Staff infra role (ownership, product & ops). For Principal/Director expectations re: fused-kernel mastery and shipping quant kernels, would want more evidence. Recommend: hire at Staff/Staff+ pending pairing result.

Notes for debrief meeting (what to lead with):
- Emphasize operational maturity, system tradeoffs, and incident storytelling.
- Flag kernel/quant gaps but frame as learnable — propose concrete validation step before leveling.

To do (my personal):
- Write up a 30-min pairing prompt focusing on one concrete misassumption: "simulate eviction under preemption and demonstrate consistent KV state with async writeback". Use GH-6189 as seed.
- Ping Maya to draft the take-home quant A/B test outline.
- Add scorecard + final comments to hiring tracker (link above) by 2025-07-22.

Random personal scratch fragments (leave):
- liked: asked about "how do you trade latency vs accuracy for logged-in power users vs free users" — shows product sense.
- didn't like: quickness to assume hardware locality when interviewer pressed on cross-AZ performance numbers.

End of scratchpad. Delete or sanitize before sharing with broader panel if we want to remove raw gut notes.
